page.layout: One column of text. Running head at top centre with page number at top right. Top: continuation of a German doxology in black letter, then a Latin paragraph in roman type. Below: an italic heading, then a German verse prayer in black letter. Signature mark at bottom centre. No marginal notes.

p.bl: Dem Herrē Gott vñ siner gnaden alle die eere/ Durch Jesum Christum/ Gott vnd mensch/ vnseren Herren.

main_text.p: In omnibus hisce versibus pedes omnes spondæi sunt, quinto excepto dactylo. Neq; fieri facile aut commodè posse opinor, utalibi etiam, nisi forte primo loco dactylus collocetur. Admittenda & licentia quædam foret præter vulgarem loquendi usum, non minùs, sed amplius forte quàm Græcis & Latinis. Nostræ quidem linguæ asperitatem consonantium etiam in eadem dict one multitudo auget, quæ nullo sæpè vocalium interventu emollitur.
main_text.head: Oratio Dominica versibus Hexametris a nobis expressa.

p.bl: O Vatter vnser/ Der du dyn ewige wonung Erhöchst inn himlen: Dyn namen werde geheilget: Zukum vns dyn rych: Dyn will der thüe beschähen / Vff erd/ als in himelen. Vnsere täglich nahrung/ Heer/ gibe vns hüt: vnnd verzych vns vnsere schulde / Wie wir verzychend jedem / Der bleidigen vns thüt. Für vns in kein versüchnuß ynChilssöne Dynen.)

main_text.p: [The first printed line of the verse prayer is in the Latin italic heading block above; no further foot notes.]

page.notes: The line "dict one" is printed with a space, probably a line-break split of "dictione"; left as printed. "ynChilssöne" is doubtful: the letters before "ssöne" are unclear, so it may be read as "vnchilssöne" or similar. Word "Dynen" is printed with a hyphen split across lines as "Dy-/nen". The black-letter "f" in "Chilssöne" and the "F" signature are as seen. Final ")" after "Dynen." is printed. The first German lines are a fragment continuing from the previous page.
